issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify lectureName as a String, but the solution repository defines the lectureName attribute as type LectureName. This introduces a cross-artifact type mismatch that will confuse students about the expected type for the attribute and whether an extra LectureName class is required.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute type consistent: either change the solution to use a String for lectureName (matching the UML and problem statement) or update the problem statement and UML to specify LectureName and document the purpose of the LectureName class. Preferably revert the solution's lectureName field to 'private String lectureName' to match the exercise specification.

issues.description: The solution's getLectureName() method declares a return type of String but returns the lectureName field of type LectureName. This will not compile and contradicts the problem's expectation of a straightforward String getter.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the getter signature with the field type. Either change the method to return LectureName (and document that in the problem statement) or change the field to String so getLectureName() can correctly return a String. Prefer changing the field to String so the getter's return type matches the UML.

issues.description: The solution's constructor accepts a LectureName parameter for lectureName, while the problem statement and UML imply the constructor should accept a String for lectureName. This mismatch creates confusion about the required constructor signature and what students must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter types consistent with the UML: change the constructor to accept a String lectureName (and initialize the field accordingly), or update the problem statement/UML to require a LectureName parameter and explain the LectureName class. The preferred fix is to change the constructor parameter to String to match the exercise description.

issues.description: The solution provides setLectureName(String) but the backing field is LectureName. The parameter type does not match the field type, which will cause assignment type errors and confuses students about the correct setter signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure setter parameter types match the field type. Either change the setter to accept a LectureName parameter or change the field to String and keep the setter accepting String. Prefer changing the field to String so setters/getters align with the problem statement and UML.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify the lectureName attribute as a String (attribute named 'lectureName: String'), but the solution introduces a new LectureName class and declares the lectureName field with type LectureName. This changes the expected identifier/type for the same conceptual entity (the lecture's name) across artifacts and creates a mapping barrier: students reading the task expect to work with a String, while the solution uses a different class name and type. Additionally, the solution contains getters/setters that appear to assume String usage while the field is LectureName, increasing confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single, consistent representation for the lecture name across all artifacts. Preferably revert the solution to use a String for lectureName (declare private String lectureName; accept a String in the constructor; remove the LectureName class) so it matches the UML and problem statement. Alternatively, if a LectureName wrapper is intended, update the problem statement and template to mention and use the LectureName class and ensure getters/setters consistently use that type.
